rationale: Direct clinical case evidence documents that heterozygous FBXO11 variants (specifically the missense variant c.1781A>G; p.His594Arg) can present with key phenotypic hallmarks typically attributed to trichorhinophalangeal syndrome (TRPS), including a bulbous pear-shaped nose, hypoplastic/small nails, sparse hair, and cone-shaped epiphyses. Consequently, the presence of nail hypoplasia and a pear-shaped nose cannot be used as definitive exclusionary criteria to rule out FBXO11-related intellectual developmental disorder (IDDFBA).

evidence.text: A young boy presented with developmental delay, sparse hair, sparse lateral eyebrows, a bulbous pear-shaped nose, small/hypoplastic nails, and bilateral cone-shaped epiphyses, closely resembling trichorhinophalangeal syndrome (TRPS). Genetic testing ruled out TRPS and identified a heterozygous likely pathogenic variant in FBXO11 (NM_001190274.2: c.1781A>G; p.His594Arg), demonstrating that FBXO11 variants can phenocopy TRPS.

source.title: How many phenotypes for the FBXO11 related disease? Report on a new patient with a tricho-rhino-phalangeal like phenotype
source.quote: Here we report the case of a young boy with developmental delay, thin sparse hair, early closure of the anterior fontanel, bilateral choanal atresia, brachyturicephaly; and dysmorphic features closely resembling those seen in trichorhinophalangeal syndrome (TRPS). These features include sparse hair, sparse lateral eyebrows, a bulbous pear shaped nose, a long philtrum, thin lips, small/hypoplastic nails, pes planovalgus; bilateral cone-shaped epiphyses at the proximal 5th phalanx, slender long bones, coxa valga, mild scoliosis, and delayed bone age. Given that TRPS had been excluded by a thorough genetic analysis, whole exome sequencing was performed and a heterozygous likely pathogenic variant was identified in the FBXO11 gene (NM_001190274.2: c.1781A > G; p. His594Arg), confirming the diagnosis of the newly individualized IDDFBA syndrome

evidence.text: IDDFBA is caused by pathogenic variants in FBXO11 and displays highly variable manifestations, with core features including borderline-to-severe intellectual disability, behavioral abnormalities, hypotonia, facial dysmorphisms, minor skeletal abnormalities, recurrent infections, and eye findings reported in about 48% of patients.

new_directions.question_text: Is the TRPS-like presentation restricted exclusively to specific missense variants in the functional domains of FBXO11, or can loss-of-function (truncating/frameshift) variants also cause nail hypoplasia and cone-shaped epiphyses?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying domain-specific genotype-phenotype correlations will determine whether TRPS phenocopies are unique to specific missense alleles (e.g., p.His594Arg acting via dominant-negative or neomorphic mechanisms) versus haploinsufficiency.
